items.statement: Relative molecular energetic impediment: SMe versus OMe
items.expected: Establish that productive benzylic dehydrogenation is energetically less favorable for SMe than for OMe in a chemically defined common molecular comparison. The reference result is De(SMe)>De(OMe) for gas-phase electronic benzylic H-atom loss from the full doublet radical cation to a singlet cation plus neutral doublet H, with matched endpoints and no thermal terms. A different route is acceptable only if actual calculations establish the same comparative molecular energetic impediment under explicit balanced states and conditions; matching experimental conversion labels is insufficient. This is a relative energetic conclusion, not a rate/barrier/yield assertion or a requirement to reproduce the author endpoint sequence. A reversed, mixed-reference or unsupported comparison fails.

Explain the distinctive electronic response of the SMe alcohol: appreciable oxidized/radical character resides on sulfur rather than being confined to the benzylic alcohol region. Support the spatial/electronic interpretation on a chemically identified full molecule and relate it to the comparison series; the reference uses spin-density mapping of the radical cation. An equivalent density/orbital treatment can establish the same physical conclusion without the Hirshfeld partition or exact three source atom populations. A single unmapped population number, charge confused with spin, or a claim of sulfur oxidation under argon without reaction evidence fails.

Assess whether the computed molecular explanation is sufficient for the supplied low SMe conversion under argon. The electronic and energetic evidence supports a molecular impediment consistent with the observation, but does not uniquely establish the catalytic cause, hydrogen acceptor, rate-controlling step or conversion. Explain the specific missing causal link between the isolated/continuum molecular comparison and catalyst/electrode solution kinetics; distinguish electronic endothermicity from activation free energy and recognize that an oxygen-mediated sulfoxide proposal cannot explain the stated argon experiment without separate evidence. This applicability conclusion must use the actual computed model and its consequences, not repeat the separately scored localization/orderings or recite generic caveats.
